previous_advisory.details: Issue summary: The QUIC stack queues a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame also for retransmitted NEW_CONNECTION_ID frames. This allows a remote malicious QUIC stack to queue an unlimited number of RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames.  Impact summary: A malicious remote QUIC peer can trigger an out-of-memory condition causing a Denial of Service.  CWE: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling  Description: The earlier fix for CVE-2026-84784 was not complete. It failed to ignore retransmissions of the NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame. The QUIC implementation created and inserted a RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frame for every retransmitted NEW_CONNECTION_ID frame it received and there was no limit on how many RETIRE_CONNECTION_ID frames were queued. This allows a malicious remote QUIC stack to trigger an out-of-memory (OOM) condition.  FIPS impact: no The FIPS module is not affected as the QUIC implementation is outside the OpenSSL FIPS module boundary.

previous_advisory.details: Issue summary: A DANE-enabled TLS client may crash by dereferencing a NULL pointer when processing an unusual combination of certificate and TLSA records.  Impact summary: The impact is limited to a client crash (potential Denial of Service).  CWE: CWE-476: NULL Pointer Dereference  Description: A DANE-enabled TLS client that supports TLSA records with at least one of the PKIX-TA(0) or PKIX-EE(1) usages alongside the DANE-TA(2) usage may crash by dereferencing a NULL pointer if the server claims a trusted CA's certificate to be its end-entity certificate and has an unusual mix of associated TLSA records.  DANE SMTP clients should not be affected since only the DANE-TA(2) and DANE-EE(3) TLSA record usages are specified applicable in SMTP.  For example, the Postfix MTA is not affected, while the Exim MTA does not at present use OpenSSL's DANE implementation.  Use of DANE in validation of RFC7250 raw public keys (RPKs) is also unaffected, as these only use DANE-EE(3) TLSA records.  Only applications that support combining the DANE PKI with a traditional PKI are potentially affected.  A DANE-enabled browser or similar, that uses OpenSSL's DANE API could be affected.  FIPS impact: no The DANE API is outside the FIPS module boundary.
